name: synergy
description: Development workflow plugin for GitHub story work and for work that stays on your machine. Say 'start the next story' and it picks an issue from your backlog, plans it, builds it, runs tests, opens a PR, has the PR reviewed independently by agents in a fresh context, and merges it on projects that turn on auto-merge. If Claude Code's auto mode blocks a run from approving or merging its own PR, the run stops cleanly and names the user setting that lets it finish. Selection reads org issue fields (Stage, Priority, Effort, Ownership) and the feature and story tree, never board cards; areas are opt-in: a project with an Areas table in ClaudeProject.md gives every issue one area label, set when it is filed or picked, and an issue needs no parent, and a scheduled board-sync keeps every issue's Stage in step. Dependencies decide order, not eligibility: a blocker inherits the priority of what waits on it, execute builds a named story's prerequisites first, and bulk-execute fills an effort budget with stories one Priority step apart, linked or not, as at most two pull requests built one after the other, in waves, and wf schedules and integrates the independent ones it builds in parallel, and orchestrate runs bulk-execute in rounds over an Epic, a Feature, a list of stories or the open pool, one round at a time, checking each against GitHub and stopping at the first sign of trouble, and it starts a round only when the Claude plan's 5-hour limit, weekly limit and budget for the day have room for it, with settings it asks each person for once. Filing an issue sets its Classification areas, and the wf CLI reads and writes issues in as few GitHub requests as it can: starting a build, opening the PR, blocking a story and cleaning up at exit are each one command that prints a one-line result when everything lands, and a run that already passed preflight skips the preflight skill. For local work, 'build this' plans, builds, verifies and commits a task or story with no issue, status or PR, then a review agent in a fresh context fixes what it finds and commits on the same branch, pr-review reviews a local change as well as a PR, verify-feature writes a short report a person reads before merging, in the chat only: a summary, a verdict, then each concern as a short question or request to the author, and it checks robustness, modularity, duplication and the repository's patterns as well as correctness, reading the parts of the system around the change and checking each concern again before it reports it, spec-hardening tests a spec against the codebase before it is built, in the chat only, and release-notes writes user and internal release notes, grouped by each issue's area label when the project uses areas, which execute and bulk-execute post on the pull request as soon as it opens, so the review checks them, and record on each story when it reaches Done, and end each run with a summary of those notes per issue; the next run writes any a merge left out, including for a pull request opened or merged outside synergy. A merged pull request also leaves each issue it closes with a release-target label, decided where the notes are written, for the project's own release script to read. It never adds AI attribution: a commit, pull request, issue or comment with a Co-Authored-By: Claude or Generated with Claude Code line is denied. It posts only to GitHub, and each session is told which platform hosts the repository; it does not check where a tool call writes, which is left to a guard on each machine. One grill skill runs every interview, and it keeps asking, in batches as large as the open questions allow, until no weak point of the plan is left. An optional jev skill says how to use Jev, the TypeSafe decision model, for quick sort, score and yes/no judgments; no workflow needs it, and when a key is set wf jev asks it nine checks: Priority, Effort, area and release targets for an issue, whether an issue is already filed, which stories are ready to build, dependencies that are probably missing, faults in a finished issue or pull request body, and which changes a user notices. Keeps what loads into each session small.
